image.alt: Arrhenius plot of ln k against 1/T showing a straight line with negative slope

explanation:
The Arrhenius equation: k = Ae^(-Ea/RT).

ln k = ln A − (Ea/R)(1/T).

This is of the form y = c + mx where:
y = ln k, x = 1/T, intercept = ln A, slope = −Ea/R.

The negative slope is confirmed physically: as 1/T increases (T decreases), k decreases.

Slope = −Ea/R.

question: (a) Distinguish between ionization energy and electron affinity giving an example in each case.
modelAnswer:
Ionization Energy: Minimum energy required to remove the outermost electron from a neutral gaseous atom.

Electron Affinity: Energy change when a neutral gaseous atom gains an electron.
Example: Cl(g) + e⁻ → Cl⁻(g), ΔH = −349 kJ/mol (exothermic for non-metals).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(b) Briefly describe and give reasons for the observed trends of the following atomic properties in the periodic table:
(i) Atomic size
(ii) Ionization energy
(iii) Electron affinity.
modelAnswer:
(i) Atomic size: Decreases across a period (increasing nuclear charge). Increases down a group (additional electron shells).

(ii) Ionization energy: Increases across a period (stronger nuclear attraction). Decreases down a group (outer electrons farther, more shielding).

(iii) Electron affinity: Generally becomes more negative across a period (increasing nuclear charge). Generally less negative down a group (larger atoms, less nuclear attraction for incoming electron).

subject: Chemistry
question:
(a) (i) Write the van der Waals equation and state all the parameters.
(ii) If sulfur (IV) oxide were an ideal gas, the pressure at 0.0°C exerted by 1.0 mole occupying 22.4L would be 1.0 atm. Use the Van der Waals equation to estimate the pressure of this volume of 1.0 mol SO2 at 0.0°C. (Take a = 6.865 L^2·atm/mol^2, b = 0.05679 L/mol.)
modelAnswer:
(i) (P + an²/V²)(V − nb) = nRT

P = pressure, V = volume, n = moles, R = gas constant, T = temperature.
a = intermolecular attraction constant.
b = molecular volume constant.

(ii) P = nRT/(V − nb) − an²/V²
nRT = 22.40 L·atm
V − nb = 22.343 L
an²/V² = 0.01368 atm

P = 22.40/22.343 − 0.01368 = 0.989 atm.

question:
(c) (i) Distinguish between natural and induced radioactivity.
(ii) The isotope 90/38 Sr is one of the extremely hazardous species in the fallout from a nuclear fission explosion. A 0.600g sample diminishes to 0.395g in ten years. Calculate the half-life.
modelAnswer:
(i) Natural radioactivity: Spontaneous decay of unstable nuclei without external stimulation.
Induced radioactivity: Radioactivity produced in stable nuclei by bombardment with high-energy particles.

(ii) N/N₀ = e^(-λt).
0.395/0.600 = e^(-10λ).
λ = 0.04185 year⁻¹.
t½ = ln2/λ = 0.6931/0.04185 = 16.6 years.

Note: The accepted literature value is ~28.8 years; this calculation uses the data given.

subject: Chemistry
question:

(ii) Using relevant illustrative reaction, distinguish between the reaction quotient (Q) and the equilibrium constant (K).
modelAnswer:
(i) The rate of a chemical reaction at constant temperature is directly proportional to the product of the molar concentrations of reactants, each raised to its stoichiometric coefficient.

(ii) For N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃:
Kc = [NH₃]²/[N₂][H₂]³ (at equilibrium).
Qc = same expression using current non-equilibrium concentrations.

If Q < K: forward reaction favoured.
If Q > K: reverse reaction favoured.
If Q = K: system at equilibrium.
